intent: The filled portion of a progress track, sized from its root's value.

dont_use_when.situation: A short busy state of unknown duration, with no percentage to measure

invariants.text: The fill's width is written inline by the primitive at runtime - a percentage between the root's `min` and `max`; progress.module.css supplies the rest - the 100% height, the color, and the width transition.
With an indeterminate root the primitive writes no width, and the stylesheet's track-keyed rule replaces the width fill with a 40%-wide sweeping band whose duration `prefers-reduced-motion` slows.

anti_patterns.dont: Set the fill's width by hand
anti_patterns.do_instead: Set the value on the root - the primitive computes the percentage and writes the width itself, so a hand-set width desyncs from the value the bar reports

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the indicator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the indicator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (status). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through progress.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A fill inside its track, beside the primitive's own root
good.code:
import { Progress as ProgressPrimitive } from '@base-ui/react/progress';

<ProgressPrimitive.Root value={64}>
  <ProgressTrack>
    <ProgressIndicator />
  </ProgressTrack>
</ProgressPrimitive.Root>

bad.title: An indicator with no progress root around it
bad.why: The indicator reads the nearest progress root's value, min and max through React context and throws when there is none; its width has no source of its own.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ProgressIndicatorState> | undefined. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the indicator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ProgressIndicatorState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc. style accepts a function of the indicator's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (status). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through progress.module.css, not through this.
